pages.name: CoreWorkPermit
pages.intent: Work permit management scaffold: a full app shell (CoreAppSidebar + CoreAppTopBar) with a single "Work Permits" sidebar entry, and a route header (PageContentHeader) carrying five tabs — Dashboard, Work Permits, Templates, Map and AI Agent (badged SOON) — plus a Settings gear as a far-right icon action. Templates is built out as the versioned template register — All/Draft/Published/Archived status tabs carrying their own counts, and a searchable, filterable DataTable with row selection, bulk delete and a New Template action in its toolbar, modelled on the Workforce Crews list. New Template and any row open the authoring page — the StateMachine widget in its work-permit variant, whose own shell supplies the Back button and hosts Discard / Save as draft / Save and publish on the far right. The other tab bodies are placeholders naming what belongs in them.
when: Starting the Work Permit product surface that owns its own app shell
A single-section app whose route content is organized by a peer tab set in the header

chooseOver.component: Assembling CoreAppSidebar + CoreAppTopBar + PageContentHeader by hand
chooseOver.because: Work Permit owns the shell and the route header, so permit surfaces plug straight in with the tab set and breadcrumb already agreed.
The two share a shell but not a tab set, and a fork would have carried Workforce's roster, settings sub-surface and ontology scope into a product that wants none of them.

pages.name: StateMachine
pages.intent: The state-machine authoring surface, whole: a header band, a left section rail, the graph on a full-bleed canvas, the editing panel beside it and a live validity footer under it. ONE widget, FOUR surfaces — two products crossed with two record ages. variant is the PRODUCT CUT (connect for WakeCap Connect V3, through ProcessDetail; work-permit for the Digital Work Permit template register) and authoring is the AGE (a record created in this session versus one that has run). Neither product owns a copy; both are callers.
when: A process, workflow or approval chain has to be drawn and edited as states and transitions
A surface needs the graph of a process alongside the panel that mutates it
An embedded read of a state machine, with shell={false} turning the chrome and the rail off

chooseOver.because: GraphCanvas draws nodes and edges; it knows nothing about states, transitions or the rules between them. This carries the domain a fresh canvas would not: the four-handle node that makes self-loops and backward edges render at all, the drag guards that refuse an illegal edge during the drag, the refusal messages quoted verbatim from checkTransition(), and the cascade when a state is deleted.

The editor lived inside the Connect V3 process page and could not be mounted anywhere else. Every graph mutation routes through a pure helper and commits with one onChange(next), so the same builder serves a page, a dialog or an embed without any of them re-deriving the rules.

requires: None — GraphCanvas wraps its own ReactFlowProvider

variantIntent.connect: WakeCap Connect V3's process page: header band, section rail (Canvas / Instances / Bottlenecks / Settings), canvas and editing panel. What ProcessDetail mounts.
variantIntent.work-permit: The Digital Work Permit cut. The same canvas, the same editing panel and the same guards — the LEFT RAIL is the whole difference today: General, Canvas, Form, Policy, then a rule, then Instances and Bottlenecks. General is the Settings section renamed, carrying the permit's type and description beside the record's own name and icon.

pages.name: CaptureUiEnhanced

Selecting a plot opens its detail; 'View blueprints' opens a per-floor sheet dialog.
when: Review a zone's approved-vs-planned construction progress on a choropleth site map
Drill a single villa/plot's milestones, per-floor progress, and reality-capture evidence
Toggle map layers (drone ortho, choropleth, roads, labels) over a weekly capture timeline

chooseOver.component: Assembling CanvasHeader + a choropleth grid + a detail rail + Collapsible layer toggles by hand
chooseOver.because: This template owns the header/breadcrumb/week-selector composition, the shared progress-bucket colour ramp across the list/map/legend, the selected-plot detail rail, and the blueprints dialog flow.
